newsitem.title: USA: Westchester County, N.Y., seeks bigger debt cap.
newsitem.headline: Westchester County, N.Y., seeks bigger debt cap.

text.p: Westchester County, New York, on Thursday said it wanted the state to approve legislation that would raise its debt cap to $25 million from $10 million.
The county, which said that it is was the only one required under state law to hold a referendum for capital project bonds over $10 million, said that the present limit, set in 1983, now was too low.

"But inflation has pushed most projects beyond that level, requiring frequent and costly referenda. Adjusted for inflation, the cap would have reached at least $25 million," Westchester County officials said, in prepared remarks.

Additionally, Westchester County sought six other measures in a package that it presented to members of the county's state delegation. The list includes asking Albany to extend a tax act that lets Westchester County share an extra one percent sales tax with communities and schools. The "Property tax Stabilization Act of 1991" is set to expire in May, 1998.
"If it isn't extended during this session, governments and school districts will have to significantly cut services or increase property taxes," the county officials warned.
--getting permanent funding for the Westchester Institute for Human Development.
--making Westchester County its own Emergency Medical Services region.
--getting the state to take over local Medicaid costs, which will cost county taxpayers $134.2 million in 1997.
--getting the state to take over Early Intervention and Preschool programs, which will cost the county $52 million in 1997.

--getting the Wick's Law changed. The law requires localities to separate construction projects that total more than $50,000. Gov George Pataki has proposed easing such restrictions, but the legislature has balked.
